units.function: Route-level tests that project create/update normalize environment bindings before persistence and restrict activity-log details to changed field names and environment variable keys.
units.dependencyDirection: Board-authenticated project HTTP routes call a Company-scoped Secret service normalizer, pass its result to the project service, and send metadata-only details to the activity logger.
units.keyDataModels: Project env map; secret_ref binding with secretId/version; plain binding with value; Company/project identity; activity details envKeys/changedKeys; project response including environment and workspace paths.
units.lifecycle: Receive environment bindings on project create or update; normalize under Company context; persist the normalized map; return the project; record only affected key names in activity metadata.
units.testAssessment: Both positive cases pass outside the restricted sandbox and the metadata-only activity-log assertion is useful. Service mocking prevents proof that normalization validates Company ownership or encrypts/rejects content. A secret-looking plain value is explicitly accepted into the persisted/returned fixture, while response redaction, read routes, rotation/revocation, runtime resolution and negative authorization/input cases are absent.
units.designRationale: Centralize environment binding normalization so routes do not implement Secret persistence details and keep raw values out of routine activity-log metadata.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must configure Agents and data connectors without placing vendor credentials in its control plane, logs, API projections or Connector contract, across managed-cloud and customer-local execution profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the Company-scoped normalization port, typed secret_ref and key-only audit metadata. Separate non-sensitive configuration from Secret bindings; reject or quarantine credential-like plain values in formal mode. Store opaque scope/version/audience references, validate ownership, resolve just in time inside the authorized execution plane, return only redacted descriptors, support rotation/revocation and ensure self-hosted/local nodes can retain secret material without sending it to cloud control.
units.responsibilityConflict: An environment map containing plaintext can silently expand an Agent's authority and leak through project reads without identifying which human granted which secret scope. Company OS must bind every secret/data grant to an accountable human, purpose, Agent/work contract, expiry and auditable revocation.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL plaintext boundary gap: the tested normalized model permits a plain value carrying secret material and the returned project fixture retains it. HIGH tenant-reference gap: no test rejects a secretId owned by another Company. HIGH response/runtime gap: API redaction, Connector exclusion, audience-limited resolution and local execution-plane custody are untested. HIGH lifecycle gap: version pinning/latest semantics, rotation, expiry, revocation and deletion are absent. MEDIUM authorization gap: an allow-all access mock reports project:read even for writes, so mutation capability fidelity is not demonstrated. POSITIVE: activity details assert environment key names rather than raw values.
